---
title: "Install MISP 3.0 on Alpine Linux 3.24"
---

This guide installs the latest [MISP `3.0_wip` branch](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/tree/3.0_wip) on a clean Alpine Linux 3.24 server.
Use the current point release of the stable series and apply its security updates. [Alpine Linux releases](https://alpinelinux.org/releases/)
The manual setup uses Apache with PHP 8.5, MariaDB 11.8, Redis, and Supervisor managed by OpenRC.
The service commands were tested in an Alpine 3.24.4 x86_64 container.

::: {.callout-note}
`3.0_wip` is the MISP 3.0 development branch.
Evaluate it on an isolated host before deployment.
Use these steps for a new database. For a MISP 2.5 instance, see [Plan a 2.5 upgrade](#alpine-install-upgrade).
:::

## Prepare the host {#alpine-install-prepare}

Run the host setup commands in a root shell.
Use a DNS name and a trusted TLS certificate and key for that name.
Restrict web access to your administration network until you change the bootstrap password.
Size the host and database storage for the expected load. [Instance requirements](../requirements/index.qmd)

Enable the `v3.24/main` and `v3.24/community` repositories in `/etc/apk/repositories`.
Install the packages and their OpenRC service definitions. Alpine packages the fuzzy-hash headers used to build `pydeep2` as `libfuzzy2-dev`. [Alpine repositories](https://wiki.alpinelinux.org/wiki/Repositories) · [libfuzzy2-dev](https://pkgs.alpinelinux.org/package/v3.24/community/x86_64/libfuzzy2-dev)

```bash
apk update
apk upgrade
apk add apache2 apache2-openrc apache2-ssl bash build-base ca-certificates \
  composer curl file git gnupg iproute2 libfuzzy2-dev \
  mariadb mariadb-client mariadb-openrc openssl procps-ng py3-pip python3-dev \
  redis redis-openrc supervisor supervisor-openrc unzip \
  php85-apache2 php85-bcmath php85-ctype php85-dom php85-fileinfo \
  php85-gd php85-intl php85-mbstring php85-openssl php85-pcntl \
  php85-pdo_mysql php85-pecl-apcu php85-pecl-redis php85-posix php85-session \
  php85-simplexml php85-tokenizer php85-xml php85-xmlreader php85-xmlwriter php85-zip
php --version
php --ri redis
php --ri pdo_mysql
mariadb --version
```

Set `memory_limit = 2048M` in `/etc/php85/conf.d/99-misp.ini` for the initial import and PHP runtime.
Alpine's default `128M` can stop `Admin updateJSON` while it loads the bundled definitions.
Check the effective setting with `php -r 'echo ini_get("memory_limit"), PHP_EOL;'`.

## Install MISP and its dependencies {#alpine-install-source}

Use the `apache` account for the checkout, dependency installation, and Cake commands.
Clone the branch with the submodules selected by the current checkout.

```bash
install -d -o apache -g apache -m 0750 /var/www/MISP /var/lib/misp \
  /var/lib/misp/composer /var/lib/misp/attachments
su -s /bin/sh apache -c 'git clone --branch 3.0_wip --recurse-submodules \
  https://github.com/MISP/MISP.git /var/www/MISP'
su -s /bin/sh apache -c 'git -C /var/www/MISP status --short --branch'
```

Install and verify the PHP and Python dependencies using the files from that checkout.

```bash
su -s /bin/sh apache -c 'export COMPOSER_HOME=/var/lib/misp/composer
  composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app install --no-dev --no-interaction --prefer-dist &&
  composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app check-platform-reqs --no-dev'
su -s /bin/sh apache -c 'export HOME=/var/lib/misp
  python3 -m venv /var/www/MISP/venv &&
  /var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python -m pip install -r /var/www/MISP/requirements.txt &&
  /var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python -m pip check'
```

## Initialize MariaDB, Redis, and MISP {#alpine-install-database}

Keep MariaDB's `skip-networking` setting in `/etc/my.cnf.d/mariadb-server.cnf` so the database is local to the host.
Keep `/etc/redis.conf` bound to loopback with protected mode enabled.
Initialize MariaDB once on the new host, start both services, and add them to the OpenRC default runlevel. [Alpine OpenRC commands](https://wiki.alpinelinux.org/wiki/OpenRC)

```bash
rc-service mariadb setup
rc-service mariadb start
rc-service redis start
rc-update add mariadb default
rc-update add redis default
redis-cli ping
MYSQL_HISTFILE=/dev/null mariadb --protocol=SOCKET
```

Redis should report `PONG` once it is ready.
In the MariaDB session, create a new database and application account.
Substitute a unique password and keep it for the MISP database settings.

```sql
CREATE DATABASE misp
    CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci;
CREATE USER 'misp'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'REPLACE_WITH_DATABASE_PASSWORD';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON misp.* TO 'misp'@'localhost';
EXIT;
```

Load the branch's MariaDB schema and copy the application configuration templates.

```bash
mariadb --protocol=SOCKET misp < /var/www/MISP/INSTALL/MARIADB.sql
for name in bootstrap config core database; do
  install -o apache -g apache -m 0640 \
    "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/$name.default.php" "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/$name.php"
done
```

In `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/database.php`, set the default connection's `login` to `misp` and `password` to the database password.
Keep `host` set to `localhost` and `database` set to `misp`.
The Alpine PHP package uses the local MariaDB socket at `/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock` for this connection.

In `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/config.php`, edit the following keys in the `MISP` section and substitute your hostname and organization.

```php
'baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'external_baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'org' => 'Your organization',
'osuser' => 'apache',
'python_bin' => '/var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python',
'attachments_dir' => '/var/lib/misp/attachments',
'redis_host' => '127.0.0.1',
'background_jobs' => false,
```

In the same file, set `Security.salt` to a unique value from `openssl rand -hex 32`.
Keep jobs disabled during initialization.
Apply the schema updates, create the first administrator, and import the bundled definitions.

```bash
su -s /bin/sh apache -c '/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin runUpdates'
(umask 077; su -s /bin/sh apache -c '/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake User init' \
  > /root/misp-bootstrap-api-key)
su -s /bin/sh apache -c '/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin updateJSON'
su -s /bin/sh apache -c '/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin schemaDiagnostics'
```

Keep the bootstrap API key private.
Confirm that the schema diagnostics show `Pending: 0` and `Failed: 0`.

### Set up the instance key {#alpine-install-gnupg}

Create the instance's GnuPG home and signing key in a private terminal.
Run the following in Bash and substitute your instance's email address.

```bash
install -d -o apache -g apache -m 0700 /var/lib/misp/gnupg
read -r -s -p 'Instance GnuPG passphrase: ' gpg_passphrase
printf '\n'
printf '%s\n' "$gpg_passphrase" | su -s /bin/sh apache -c \
  'gpg --homedir /var/lib/misp/gnupg --batch --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase-fd 0 \
  --quick-generate-key misp@example.org ed25519 sign never'
unset gpg_passphrase
su -s /bin/sh apache -c 'gpg --homedir /var/lib/misp/gnupg --armor --export \
  misp@example.org > /var/www/MISP/app/webroot/gpg.asc'
```

Set `GnuPG.homedir`, `GnuPG.email`, and `GnuPG.password` in `app/Config/config.php` to the directory, email address, and passphrase you used.
Include the private key and configuration in your protected backups. [Instance and user keys](../cryptographic-keys/index.qmd)

## Serve MISP over HTTPS {#alpine-install-web}

Uncomment the `LoadModule rewrite_module` line in `/etc/apache2/httpd.conf`.
Keep the `headers` module and the prefork MPM enabled for the packaged PHP module.
In `/etc/apache2/conf.d/ssl.conf`, replace the packaged example `<VirtualHost>` block with the following.
Keep the global TLS settings, including `Listen 443`, and use your actual hostname and certificate paths.

```apache
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName misp.example.org
    Redirect permanent / https://misp.example.org/
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName misp.example.org
    DocumentRoot /var/www/MISP/app/webroot
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /etc/ssl/certs/misp-fullchain.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/ssl/private/misp.key

    <Directory /var/www/MISP/app/webroot>
        Options -Indexes +FollowSymLinks
        AllowOverride FileInfo
        Require all granted
        DirectoryIndex index.php
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
```

Allow the rewrite and authorization rules in `app/webroot/.htaccess` through `AllowOverride FileInfo`.
Check the Apache configuration and start the service.

```bash
rc-service apache2 configtest
rc-service apache2 start
rc-update add apache2 default
```

From a trusted client, confirm that HTTP redirects to HTTPS, verify the certificate, and sign in as `admin@admin.test` with password `admin`.
Change the password before opening the site to other clients. [First steps after login](../quick-start/index.qmd#first-steps-after-login)

## Start and verify the workers {#alpine-install-workers}

Use Supervisor's local Unix socket for worker management.
Edit the existing `[unix_http_server]` section of `/etc/supervisord.conf` and keep the packaged `[rpcinterface:supervisor]` and `[supervisorctl]` sections.
Grant access to the `apache` group and leave the TCP management listener disabled.

```ini
[unix_http_server]
file=/run/supervisord.sock
chmod=0660
chown=root:apache
```

Create a Supervisor worker group with one process per queue and one dedicated scheduler.

```bash
install -d -m 0755 /etc/supervisor.d
{
  printf '%s\n' '[group:misp-workers]' \
    'programs=default,email,cache,prio,update,scheduler'
  for worker in default email cache prio update scheduler; do
    if [ "$worker" = scheduler ]; then
      cake_command=scheduler_worker
    else
      cake_command="start_worker $worker"
    fi
    cat <<EOF

[program:$worker]
command=/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake $cake_command
directory=/var/www/MISP
user=apache
autostart=true
autorestart=true
redirect_stderr=true
stdout_logfile=/var/www/MISP/app/tmp/logs/$worker-worker.log
EOF
  done
} > /etc/supervisor.d/misp-workers.ini
```

In the `SimpleBackgroundJobs` section of `app/Config/config.php`, set `redis_host` to `127.0.0.1` and `supervisor_host` to `unix:/run/supervisord.sock`.
Set `supervisor_user` and `supervisor_password` to empty strings for this socket configuration.
Set `MISP.background_jobs` to `true` and start Supervisor.

```bash
rc-service supervisord start
rc-update add supervisord default
supervisorctl status 'misp-workers:*'
su -s /bin/sh apache -c '/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin getWorkers'
rc-status default
ss -lnt
```

Confirm that all six processes are running, Redis listens only on loopback, and MariaDB and Supervisor have no TCP listeners in this setup.
Save and search for an unpublished, organization-only event and verify that a queued job finishes before enabling synchronization or scheduled feeds. [Background worker checks](../administration/index.qmd#admin-background-jobs)

## Plan a 2.5 upgrade {#alpine-install-upgrade}

For an existing MISP 2.5 instance, follow the [offline database upgrade](../upgrade-2-5-to-3-0/index.qmd) for backups, staging, and validation.
Use the `apache` account for the MISP commands and the same `misp-workers` group for Supervisor.
Restart the packaged PHP module with `rc-service apache2 restart` after the migration.
Time the `Admin runUpgrade` operation on a restored copy to estimate your maintenance window.
